tagline: The bareboat-charter heartland of the Mediterranean — a dense island archipelago off a single hub city.
summary: Split is the charter capital of the Adriatic: the central Dalmatian islands (Hvar, Brač, Šolta, Vis) sit a short hop offshore, served by Jadrolinija ferries and Krilo/Kapetan Luka catamarans and one of the densest bareboat- and crewed-charter fleets in the Med (ACI marina network). Distances are short, the water is sheltered by the island chain, and summer road/ferry congestion makes a fast premium water tier compelling.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II owns the entire central-Dalmatian mesh — Hvar (~22 nm), Brač (~15 nm), Šolta, Vis (~30 nm) — and all charter-base tenders.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR (H2 2026+) links Split south to Dubrovnik and the Elaphiti/Korčula chain.

competitive_landscape: Jadrolinija ferries, Krilo/Kapetan Luka catamarans and a vast charter fleet operate today — deep demand proof and partners (ACI marinas). Summer catamaran sell-outs are the clear pain. No foiling incumbent.
seasonality: Strongly seasonal (Jun–Sep peak); shoulder months viable on the sheltered island-protected water.
regulatory_note: Croatian flag / EU; Croatian Register of Shipping; ACI is the dominant marina operator and a natural berth partner. EU cabotage applies.

precedents.why_it_matters: Split plays the same single-hub-plus-dense-islands charter role.
